title: TUI integration edit: restore the kind slot when switching back to the original kind
description: In the integration edit dense form, changing the kind clears the kind slot (base URL / command / MCP URL) so an old value is never sent under the wrong flag (v1.16.0). Switching back to the original kind leaves the slot empty instead of restoring the stored value; the operator must re-open the row and retype it. Fix: remember the stored slot per kind and restore it when the kind returns to the record's kind. Files: internal/tui/integration_views.go (slotRows/slotValue), internal/tui/list_remove_views.go (integration edit).

title: Approval requests must reach the operator (not depend on the agent relaying a QR)
description: When a print approval fires in a non-tty agent context, the QR / tunnel URL goes to the agent's stderr; Honey didn't relay it and it timed out. Notify the admin directly (desktop notification; optional Buzz/Mattermost hook) and print a one-line instruction for agents: 'ask your operator to approve: <url>'. Show pending print approvals in the TUI.

title: Track _rules/ encrypted with git-crypt (restores devlog hook)
description: _rules/ is gitignored, so the bd pre-commit devlog check can never pass; commits use --no-verify meanwhile (devlog still recorded locally first). Plan: brew install git-crypt; git-crypt init; .gitattributes '_rules/** filter=git-crypt diff=git-crypt'; drop /_rules/ from .gitignore; re-add _rules/; store the exported key in DOP + a backup. Verify on a branch that GitHub shows _rules/ as encrypted before merging. History is already purged of plaintext _rules (2026-10-08).

title: Claimed agents never need re-approval: exec is the identity path (restart / any harness)
description:
Principle (operator, 2026-10-08): an agent that has claimed a bearer must not need a new approval after a restart, in Buzz or any harness. The claimed key on its machine IS its identity ('default' fixed identity), unlike portable bearers (dop use), which keep per-session approval.

Today: `dop exec` already has NO approval gate (printguard is only in runEnv / runUse / runClaim / issueBearer). Honey (Buzz) hit approvals only because it used `dop env` (a print surface) and then `dop use` (portable-only), after a restart reset its trust context (kind: sid, a new shell per tool call).

To do (discuss first):
1. Make exec the obvious path for claimed bearers: when `dop env` / `dop use` is called with a claimed (bound) bearer, say so and point to `dop exec --agent-name <name> -- <cmd>` (no approval needed) before or instead of firing approval.
2. Decide on `dop env` for claimed bearers: keep it gated (it prints raw keys into the agent shell — recommended), or allow it when the agent proves its key? Open question.
3. Verify exec after a restart needs zero config: bearer discovery (DOP_TOKEN / token file written at claim?), key load (SE / file) without prompts.
4. e2e: claim → new process / new session id → dop exec works, no approval event in the audit log.
5. Docs + skill: claimed → exec; portable → use; never eval "$(dop env)".
design:
DECISION (operator, 2026-10-08) — fixed identity must be seamless; printing stays gated when there's no proof.

1. Claimed (bound) bearer + proof of key possession → no approval, no passphrase, ever:
   - dop exec: already approval-free (keep).
   - dop env: allowed WITHOUT approval when the agent proves it holds the bound key — same signed-challenge proof exec uses (P-256 SE/file or ed25519 per binding.key_type), checked against the admin-signed record. Works across restarts and any harness (Buzz, Claude Code, opencode…), independent of the trust-context cache.
2. No proof → gated behind approval (popup / phone / passphrase), as today:
   - unclaimed / unbound (--no-bind) bearers, proof fails or key missing, and portable recall (dop use: the admin's own bearer in any shell — keeps per-session approval via the trust context).
3. Printing is never needed to *use* DOP (exec covers it), so the gate stays the default for every print surface without proof; the proof path is the only bypass besides DOP_FROM_TUI.
4. Audit: log env prints granted by key proof (print_approval_granted, channel=key_proof, lookup prefix) so they stay traceable.

Open: dop claim's own export line (one-time, at claim) — keep gated or allow once the binding is confirmed? Default: allow (the agent just proved the key during claim).
notes:
INVARIANT (operator, 2026-10-08): the FIRST CLAIM always requires admin approval (QR → phone, or system prompt window). It is the human check 'I gave this agent its claim command and it is claiming now'. An unexpected approval request = someone else claiming → refuse. Key proof can never replace it: at claim time the key is brand new and unvouched. Key-proof bypass applies only AFTER the claim is approved (exec, dop env with proof). The 'open' item about the claim export line means only the post-approval print — not the claim approval itself; default: no second prompt right after the admin approved.

EVIDENCE (Honey, Buzz, 2026-10-08): with the trust-context cache, a claimed agent costs one approval per new session id (random sid each tool call → one per call; a stable DOP_SESSION_ID → one per conversation, 30m idle). The operator typed the passphrase twice in one morning for an agent claimed the day before. Target: zero after the claim.
close_reason: Claimed agents: dop env with key proof + approved-claim export print without prompts; dop use → exec hint; docs. e2e v1_1700.

title: TUI UX critique — Impeccable dual-agent synthesis (A+B) on internal/tui/
description:
# TUI UX critique synthesis (Impeccable dual-agent run on `internal/tui/`)

**Method:** dual-agent (A: `a8a4a03d7eb515ee3` · B: `a45828ce12c84bc07`)
**Target:** `internal/tui/` · **Slug:** `internal-tui`
**Platform:** Go / Bubble Tea TUI (text-only; Impeccable visual-pixel judgments mapped to text-cell equivalents)
**Date of run:** 2026-10-05

---

## Design Health Score

| # | Nielsen Heuristic | Score | Primary observation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Visibility of system status | **3/4** | State line + pending banner + flash + live-tail during invite are strong. No live session-TTL countdown. |
| 2 | Match with real world | **3/4** | Operator vocabulary mostly natural; `KindSlot` / `generation` / `cap-id prefix` leak into help text. |
| 3 | User control & freedom | **2/4** | `esc` behavior inconsistent across views; "any key" dismisses the one-time-shown bearer on issue success. |
| 4 | Consistency & standards | **2/4** | 6+ picker idioms diverge on `space`/`a`/`n`/`other…`/backspace semantics. rc7l fixed Settings; the rest weren't converged. |
| 5 | Error prevention | **3/4** | Env-prefix collision warning + "passphrase matches admin passphrase" check + shared-identity ⚠ are excellent. |
| 6 | Recognition rather than recall | **2/4** | Owner glyphs (👤 🔒 p.) have no in-view legend; preset labels (`"1h (default — chat-friendly)"`) are a bright spot. |
| 7 | Flexibility & efficiency | **3/4** | j/k + arrows + 1-5 + single-letter + tab = real veteran paths. No fuzzy search with 50+ integrations. |
| 8 | Aesthetic & minimalist | **2/4** | Add-integration shows 11 rows + conditional pickers + hints + Save + error line + footer, often simultaneously. |
| 9 | Error recovery | **3/4** | `guardAdminAction` + osascript unlock + pending-fn stash is elegant. Loses a point: raw Go stderr surfaces to users. |
| 10 | Help & documentation | **2/4** | Footer-only. No `?`, no in-TUI concept docs. Admin/agent model is nowhere surfaced. |

**Mean: 2.5** — competent, inconsistent, dense.

**Design specificity:** domain-aware in the leaves (ownership glyphs, protected-grant passphrase sub-step, auto-reseal watcher, shared-identity warning), **generic at the trunk** (number menu, standard footer, muted state line, brand/muted/ok/danger palette). The admin-plane / agent-plane / operator-at-terminal / operator-at-phone split that is DOP's whole premise is nowhere visualized in the chrome.

---

## Cognitive load

- **Add-integration** = 11 rows with hidden-state branching (kind choice mutates subsequent step labels, no breadcrumb). A → "needs decomposition into quick-add + optional advanced-later." B → `integration_views.go` is 1548 LOC, split candidate. **Agree.**
- **Issue token** = step counter `0,1,2,3,4,100` with sentinel; user never sees "step N of M."
- **Bearer list** = 8 modes + two-phase grant-pick + modal transitions inferred from footer changes.
- **Muscle memory burden:** `a` means **four different things** across views (bulk-select / approve pending / show-all-revoked / toggle in grant-pick). B's step-literal scan (10 `step == N` sites, 7 in `views.go`) confirms the drift surface A described — same anti-pattern class as the rc6m bug.

---

## Emotional journey (peak-end)

| Flow | Start | Middle | End |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Admin init** | Calm | Anxious — 4 passphrase fields, "must be different" lands after typing | Mild dread if login step fails (bad landing) |
| **Add integration** | Curious | **Swamped** (11 rows, hidden-state branching, 6-field advanced sub-form) | Satisfying — probe summary + ✓ |
| **Issue token** | Energetic (env-prefix collision warning is 🤌) | Good | **High-stakes anxiety — "any key" dismisses bearer forever** |
| **Invite teammate** | Calm (fire-and-forget framing is honest) | Good (live tail transparent) | **Strongest end in the TUI** — exact read-aloud incantation + unambiguous enter/esc |

---

## Strengths (what to protect)

1. **Env-prefix collision warning** in the issue grant picker. Real-time, specific, prevents a silent "last write wins" footgun. Only exists because someone was burned.
2. **`guardAdminAction` + osascript unlock pattern** (rc7h). The pending-fn stash is a beautiful solution to "re-prompt mid-flow without blowing up the event loop."
3. **Invite waiting screen** (rc7o). Specific read-aloud incantation + unambiguous "enter closes / esc cancels." Peak collaborative moment.

---

## Priority issues (A findings; B provides mechanical corroboration)

### 1. Bearer loss on stray keypress — `views.go:512-517` (issue step 100)
"Any key dismisses" + "shown ONCE" + no re-copy = foot-gun. Needs explicit "I've saved it" confirm + `c` to re-copy before dismiss.
*A only — B's grep can't see this; it's behavioral.*

### 2. Picker idiom divergence
Settings view's rc7l rewrite documented the problem AND solved it only for Settings. The same sweep is overdue for `issueView`, `addIntegrationView`, `listView` grant-pick.
**B's evidence:** 29 ad-hoc `lipgloss.NewStyle` call sites outside the shared palette → the inconsistency extends from behavior to visual.

### 3. Add-integration maximalism
`integration_views.go` is 1548 LOC (B) hosting 11 rows + 4 conditional branches (A). Decompose into "quick add" + optional "advanced details" entry on the saved view.

### 4. Raw error surfacing
Operators see stripped Go stderr. B found **34 duplicated `if v.err != ""` render sites** → single `friendlyize(err)` helper would land once across all 34.

### 5. No live session-TTL countdown
State line is paint-time, not live. `guardAdminAction` exists specifically to cover for a status display that should have prevented the surprise in the first place.

---

## Mechanical findings (B-only, no A overlap)

- **Three files exceed 1500 LOC**: `list_remove_views.go` 2828, `views.go` 2275, `integration_views.go` 1548. Together 43% of the package.
- **2 `strings.Repeat(" ", …)` padding sites** in `tui.go:584, 670` — **direct violation of Contract 14** ("MUST use `lipgloss.Width()`" line 76-77). Localized, fixable in one patch.
- **10 `step == N` literal comparisons** concentrated in `views.go` (7 of 10). Any step shift re-triggers the rc6m bug. Named-constant sweep overdue.
- **2 Sprintf chains with ≥4 `%s`** at `views.go:2026` (bearer metadata status bar) and `list_remove_views.go:600` (token row) — formatting-helper candidates.
- **Totals:** 11,985 LOC in 19 files, 410 functions / 71 structs.

---

## Agreement vs divergence

| Finding | A | B | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Picker idiom divergence (behavior) | ✅ | — | A behavioral; B infrastructural (`lipgloss.NewStyle` sprawl) |
| Error surfacing is raw | ✅ | ✅ (34 sites) | Agree — fix is a shared helper |
| Hidden-state branching in step models | ✅ | ✅ (10 literal `step==N`) | Agree — same anti-pattern class as rc6m |
| Add-integration is maximalist | ✅ | ✅ (1548 LOC) | Agree |
| Three oversized files | — | ✅ | B-only; A didn't quantify |
| Bearer loss on stray keypress | ✅ | — | A-only; behavioral, not grep-able |
| Emotional journey valleys | ✅ | — | A-only |

**No false positives from B**; A didn't contradict any mechanical finding.

---

## Persona red flags

- **New team member joining** → waiting-screen hint ("open List → Team → Pending press `a`") is good, but no proactive banner on the next menu reopen that says "you have a pending approval."
- **Veteran admin issuing 100th token** → 5-page wizard for the common case. Needs a "quick issue" one-liner mode.
- **Operator with 50+ integrations** → add-grant integration picker has no search/filter; arrow-key only.

---

## Minor observations

- `looksLikePIN` and `extractRepinPin` scrape CLI stdout via string matching — fragile; a CLI output format change silently breaks TUI PIN display.
- `flashMessage` is one-shot; also used for guard-unlock status messages which the operator might blink past.
- Settings-view's rc7l docstring is a design document living in code. Great discipline — but only applies to that one view.
- Protection passphrase shows masked dots but no live min-chars feedback until enter.

---

## Three provocative questions

1. **Why is this a modal TUI at all?** The CLI is the source of truth; every TUI action shells out. What would a *dashboard* (persistent, live-updating list with inline action keys — no screen stack) feel like compared to the current wizard model?
2. **What's the TUI's answer to "I just made a mistake"?** No visible undo, no history. For a tool whose premise is "revoke is easy, so you can issue freely" — why is the TUI silent about the fact that revoke IS the undo?
3. **If a new team member watches a veteran admin use the TUI, can they learn by observation?** Most interactions are invisible single-keys (`a`, `r`, `d`, `+`, `p`). Should every keypress flash its name at the top-right for 500ms?

---

## Impeccable fit note

DOP TUI is terminal-only — Impeccable's detector returned zero findings (nothing to inspect in Go). The adapted mechanical scans (`go vet`, grep patterns, LOC footprint) + the design-director Assessment A carried the critique. Impeccable's visual-pixel discipline doesn't translate; its heuristic framework does.

---

## Suggested next-session menu

Pick one when resuming:

1. **Bearer-loss foot-gun** on issue-success "any key" (`views.go:512-517`)
2. **Picker idiom sweep** across remaining non-Settings views (`issueView`, `addIntegrationView`, `listView` grant-pick)
3. **Add-integration decomposition** (quick-add + advanced-later) — splits the 1548 LOC file naturally
4. **Shared `friendlyize(err)` helper** + 34 render-site rewrite
5. **Live session-TTL countdown** in the state line
close_reason: Addressed by v1.16.0 (PR #1): one frame + short footer + ? help on every screen, Esc one level back everywhere, picker idioms unified on one multi-select and one dense-form helper, Add integration decomposed into the Integration › Credential › Grant stepper with Normal/Advanced, step counters on wizards, issue-success bearer guard (enter / esc twice / c copy), vocabulary and glyph cleanup, stderr mapped through cliErr, screen-walk harness enforcing the layout rules. Remaining small gaps filed as separate issues.

title: TUI: a description cannot be cleared from the edit forms (CLI keeps existing on empty)
description: dop integration add merges into an existing integration and keeps the existing description when given an empty one (cmd/dop/integrationcmd.go, runIntegrationAdd merge rules), so the TUI edit form cannot clear a description. Options: an explicit --clear-description flag (or --description= sentinel) on the CLI, and the TUI sends it when the row is emptied. Same question for projects/tags if they follow the same rule; verify.

title: Phone as approver: signed approvals from an iOS app, relay wake-ups
description: Design in docs/08-phone-approver.md (branch design/phone-approver). The phone pairs as a device with a Secure Enclave P-256 key; approvals are signatures gated by Face ID or the passphrase typed on the phone; the vault repo is the bus (pending-approvals/ request + decision records); a Cloud Run relay holds the APNs key and only carries 'something is waiting'. Passphrase on the Mac / web page stays as the fallback. v1 = control and validation: pending list across claim / remote-claim / print-bearer / print-keys / protected-grant, approve/reject, history. Absorbs dop-5j8 (reach the operator) and dop-dkj (per-kind presentation).

title: Align passphrase prompts: rename-token on a protected integration asks the approval passphrase, set-token does not
description: dop integration rename-token (v1.16.0) gates a protected integration with the owner check AND the approval passphrase because it rewrites grants; dop integration set-token only does the owner check (contract 18 says set-token must not re-prompt). Decide one rule for credential mutations on protected integrations and apply it to both (and to the TUI Rename action on the Credentials tab, which shows the passphrase step only in that case). Files: cmd/dop/integrationcmd.go, internal/tui/list_remove_views.go, contract 18.

title: Approval dialog redesign: make what's at stake obvious
description: Approval popups / phone page look the same whether an agent is claiming (expected after you gave a claim command) or a command wants to PRINT keys into a transcript. Rework message, colour, icon per surface: claim (identity), print bearer, print keys (highest risk, red), protected grant. Say who asks (subject, agent name, host, harness), what will happen ('keys will be shown in an AI transcript'), and the safe alternative (dop exec). Consider refusing instead of prompting where printing is never needed (done for bound dop env).

title: Rotate keys exposed on 2026-10-08 (Notion via opencode history; BuzzReaders bearer)
description: 1) Two distinct Notion keys landed in ~/.local/share/opencode (opencode.log, opencode.db) and at the model provider — the BuzzReaders grants (Outgrey workspace, 'Agent grant access' bot). Rotate at Notion, then dop integration set-token. Honey also used two Boiler tokens (skills registry, pensieve) — no scan pattern for them, rotate to be safe. 2) dop token rotate BuzzReaders — its full bearer was printed into a Claude Code transcript during the investigation (claimed/bound, so low risk). Optional: purge the opencode log/db entries locally (provider copy can't be deleted).

title: Rename a bearer (subject) in place
description: Next round. Bearer subjects can't be renamed today (integrations, credentials and grants can). Add dop token rename + TUI Rename on the bearer detail; keep lookup id / binding / claim; audit; mind --agent-name matching subjects on the bearer-free path.

title: Rotate / re-issue a bearer without a new claim — cover every binding
description: Next round. Claimed P-256 bearers already rotate in place (BearerWrapped, key re-tagged, no reclaim). Gaps: ed25519 (incl. every claim --remote, see dop-ynw) must revoke + reissue + reclaim; unbound/portable re-issue paths; TUI exposure of rotate. Goal: an admin can replace a bearer value (e.g. after a leak) with zero agent-side ceremony whenever the agent has a key.
notes: 2026-10-10: claim --remote now generates P-256 by default (dop-ynw), so new remote bearers rotate in place like local ones; the ed25519 gap is now only pre-existing bindings. Remaining: unbound (--no-bind) re-issue.

title: Harden print approval: agent-set DOP_SESSION_ID + DOP_APPROVAL_PASSPHRASE exposure
description:
Honey (Buzz) reported that after setting its own DOP_SESSION_ID, `eval "$(dop env)"` resolved 'silently from the trust cache — no phone prompt'. A newly invented session id shouldn't match any cached grant (keyed on (kind, value, subject)), so either DOP_APPROVAL_PASSPHRASE is in the agent's env (a silent scripted bypass), an approval did land, or there's a cache bug.

To do: read Honey's host audit log (print_approval_granted: channel trust_context vs passphrase vs phone) for 2026-10-08 ~11:50. Make sure an agent-controlled env can't self-approve: DOP_APPROVAL_PASSPHRASE should never be reachable by an agent (document it; consider refusing it when a harness/agent context is detected); confirm DOP_SESSION_ID alone grants nothing new.
notes: FINDING (2026-10-08, Honey's account + operator memory): NO silent bypass. Operator typed the approval passphrase twice: ~09:44 (random sid context) and ~09:53 (Honey's own DOP_SESSION_ID → kind explicit, new context). Everything after reused the cached grant (dop trust list: context explicit, value honey-buzz-dm-…, subject BuzzReaders, 30m idle TTL) — working as designed. Downgraded P1 → P3. Remaining hardening: (1) an agent-chosen DOP_SESSION_ID is fine (first use still needs approval) but document that the grant follows whoever reuses that id for 30m; (2) make sure DOP_APPROVAL_PASSPHRASE can never be reachable by an agent (docs; consider refusing it when an agent/harness context is detected).

title: Keep keys out of captured agent output (env refusal + exec masking)
description:
Evidence 2026-10-08: Honey (opencode) ran DOP_TOKEN=… dop env 18× (approved twice by the operator); the output put Notion keys in model context, the model wrote one literally in a curl command, logged by opencode (opencode.log ×3, opencode.db ×9) and sent to the provider. Colleague's point: printed = sent + kept in harness history.
Fix (branch fix/agent-key-exposure): (1) dop env refused outright for a bound/claimed bearer when stdout is captured, unless explicit scripted admin approval (DOP_APPROVAL_PASSPHRASE); audit env_denied bound_bearer_print_refused; the v1.18-rc1 key-proof bypass removed. (2) dop exec masks injected key values (‹NAME›) in captured stdout/stderr before the terminal; real tty unchanged; exit code + signals forwarded. (3) Docs: threat model 'Printed means sent', CLI reference, agentic hubs, feature sheet.
close_reason: Shipped in v1.18.0: dop env refused for claimed agents in captured output; exec masks injected keys

title: dop skills: claimed → dop exec, portable → dop use, never eval dop env
description: The dop-use / dop-credential-access skills steer agents to eval "$(dop use X)" regardless of bearer type; Honey reached for dop use on a claimed bearer 'out of habit from the skill file', then settled on eval "$(dop env)" (puts raw keys in the agent shell). Rewrite the guidance: detect the bearer type (dop whoami / token show), use `dop exec --agent-name <name> -- <cmd>` for claimed bearers, `dop use` only for portable ones, never `eval "$(dop env)"`; when an approval fires, relay the URL to the operator immediately.
notes: Add (2026-10-08 evidence): agents must never write a key literally in a command — reference $NAME inside dop exec -- sh -c '…' so the shell expands it. dop env is refused for claimed agents (dop-q49). Relay approval URLs to the operator.
close_reason: Skill rewritten: bearer-kind table (claimed → dop exec, portable → dop use, unbound → DOP_TOKEN), after-claim section, never eval dop env, reference $NAME in the child. Commit on feature/ci-runner.

title: Buzz harness adapter for the trust-context cache
description: DOP recognizes Claude Code / Codex / opencode sessions so one approval covers a whole conversation. Buzz isn't recognized → falls back to kind: sid (a new shell per tool call → an approval per call for dop use / dop env). Add a Buzz adapter (find the per-agent/conversation session env var Buzz exposes), plus Settings › Harness entry. Also consider Berd. Matters for portable/print surfaces; claimed exec is covered by dop-8g7.

title: Keys leak through pseudo-terminals (Cursor / node-pty): mask regardless of isatty
description: Teammate report 2026-10-09, reproduced: dop exec masks only when stdout/stderr aren't terminals; harnesses running agent commands in a PTY (Cursor, VS Code via node-pty, script, expect) capture the key in clear → sent to the model API. e2e v1_1820_terminal_leak_matrix: 7/16 cases LEAK; real node-pty: printenv/env/curl -v → LEAK. dop env with a bound bearer under a pty reaches the approval dialog instead of being refused. Branch fix/terminal-masking. Proposal: pty proxy (creack/pty) so masking is unconditional; refuse dop env for bound bearers regardless of tty; matrix as regression gate; document limits.
notes: 2026-10-10: real node-pty 1.1.0 (Node 26) re-run on v1.18.2 build: exec printenv / env dump / bearer-free printenv under node-pty → masked; env (bound) → refused; 0 leaks in 5 cases. node-pty scratch install removed afterwards.
close_reason: Verified on main at v1.18.2 (merge 59c7243): v1_1820_terminal_leak_matrix → 0 leaks in 18 cases (pipe/pty/mixed, script(1), expect, sandbox without pty, --inherit-env, bearer-free); dop env for bound bearers refused under pipe and pty. Fix shipped from fix/terminal-masking (pty proxy + sandbox fallback).

title: Projects / tags on an integration cascade to its grants (inherit on read)
description:
Integration.Projects/Tags were added in v1.14.0-rc3 as grouping metadata with no inheritance to grants. Result: tagging an integration does nothing functional — token issue --project/--tags and the TUI grouping read grant-level fields only.

Decision (2026-10-10): cascade by inheriting on read, not by copying on write. A grant's effective projects/tags = union(grant's own, its integration's). No duplicated data, no cascade writes, integration edits visible instantly, grants can still add narrower labels. A grant cannot exclude an inherited project (union semantics); move the credential to its own integration instead.

Scope: Grant.EffectiveProjects(v)/EffectiveTags(v) helpers; switch the ~29 read sites (token issue filter, integration detail, grant list, TUI detail/grouping) to them; show inherited labels muted in the grant detail; e2e for the issue filter. Write paths unchanged.

title: README rewrite — TUI-first, landing-page feature blocks with GIFs
description: Rewrite README TUI-first in landing-page 'features' style: short blocks each illustrated by a VHS GIF, one CLI pointer line per feature, ~half the text (863 → ~420 words). Full proposal, mock README, GIF specs, where-the-cut-text-goes table and open questions: _rules/_plans/readme-tui-first-landing.md (local, gitignored). First step: spike VHS against a fixture HOME running the real binary.
close_reason: TUI-first README with tour GIF merged to main

title: Bubble Tea init queries the terminal (OSC 11 + cursor report) on every dop launch
description: bubbletea v1 tea_init.go calls lipgloss.HasDarkBackground() at package init, so every dop invocation (exec, --version…) sends OSC 11 + DSR to the terminal and waits up to termenv's OSC timeout (5 s) for the reply, reading stdin. Real terminals (xterm.js in Cursor/VS Code, iTerm, Terminal.app) answer at once → harmless; a pty that never answers (expect, some test harnesses) loses keystrokes typed in the first seconds. Found 2026-10-09 while testing the pty proxy (dop-v5s). Options: move the TUI behind a lazily imported entry (keep bubbletea out of non-TUI command paths), or bubbletea v2 (removes the workaround). main()-level lipgloss.SetHasDarkBackground is too late (runs after package init).

title: e2e scripts: stop killing every dop session daemon on the machine
description: 8 scripts in testdata/e2e end with `pkill -9 -f "dop admin __session-daemon"`, which also kills the developer's real admin session (and other tests' daemons). Replace with `"$DOP" admin logout` in the script's HOME (or kill by the test socket path) in a cleanup trap. Hit on 2026-10-08 while running v1_env_binding.sh — the operator's real session ended up locked.

title: Switch vault — per-vault profiles (agents keep working across a switch)
description: Parked until real demand. Profiles = separate DOP roots (builds on DOP_HOME); agents route by bearer (search all profiles' capabilities/), never by the admin's current profile; each vault keeps its own daemon so switching doesn't lock the other. TUI: header vault chip + More › Vaults (switch/add/remove). First step if picked up: bearer routing across profiles in exec/env/use. Full design: _rules/_plans/vault-switch-profiles.md (local).

title: Remote server / agent-join flow: bring to parity with P-256, direct availability, TUI
description:
The server-side join path lags the local claim path.

Gaps found (2026-10-08):
- `dop claim --remote` (runClaimRemote, cmd/dop/claimcmd.go) always generates an ed25519 key. No P-256 (SE on macOS, file-backed P-256 on Linux with DOP_ALLOW_FILE_KEYS=1, no `--key-type`), so remote-claimed bearers can't use direct availability: add-grant / remove-grant / reseal / rotate (EnvWrapped / BearerWrapped need P-256 ECDH, v1.12).
- `dop approve-remote` is CLI-only. The TUI has no screen or pending indicator for staged remote claims (pending-remote-claims/ in the vault repo); invites have a Team › Pending tab, remote claims don't.
- The server needs pull and push on the vault repo (claim --remote stages and pushes the claim). Not documented as a prerequisite.
- docs/01-onboarding.md still says 'cross-host claim is on the roadmap' (stale); no 'Remote server' section. docs/06-ci-headless.md covers pre-paired / unbound but not claim --remote.
- Orphan agent keys after revoke accumulate on the server (auto-cleaned only when revoke runs on the same host); only `dop agent sweep` cleans them.

Plan to scope:
1. claim --remote: key-type parity with local claim (auto: SE → P-256 file opt-in → ed25519 fallback), `--key-type p256`, binding.key_type in the staged bundle.
2. approve-remote: seal EnvWrapped on approval for P-256 bindings so direct availability works from day one.
3. TUI: pending remote claims surfaced (banner + list + approve/reject), reusing the Team › Pending pattern.
4. Optional: agent-side orphan sweep on exec/pull for headless hosts.
5. Docs: 'Remote server' section in onboarding (attach as agent, deploy key with push, issue, claim --remote, approve), fix the stale roadmap line, cross-link 06-ci-headless.
6. e2e: extend v1_remote_claim.sh for P-256 + add-grant after a remote claim.
